The landlord says the increase is because of renovation and value-enhancing investment work on the building.
Landlord: Wohnbau Limmat GmbH. Tenant: Taylor Brooks. Rented property: 3.5-room flat, Gartenweg 54, Frauenfeld, Switzerland.
Start date of tenancy: 1 April 2014. Agreed net rent: CHF 1760 per month, plus ancillary costs as separately stated.

plan.because: The supplied agreement identifies the contracting parties and property and states the tenancy start date and agreed net rent.
The notice is reported but not supplied; the original is needed to assess its amount, effective date, addressee and form contents.
Receipt is reported, but no evidence establishes the recipient and evidenced delivery date for deadline assessment.
The lease states net rent and refers to ancillary costs separately, but does not establish all current rent components.
No prior adjustment evidence is supplied; the previous adjustment date, amount and calculation basis are needed.
The increase letter is not supplied, and the stated reasons and calculation inputs are needed to assess the increase.
The claim leaves open whether the increase is based on the reference rate; request this evidence after clarifying the basis.
Renovation is stated as a reason, but no evidence of the works, costs or claimed allocation to rent is supplied.
This document type is optional under the process rules.

questions: Does the landlord rely on the reference-rate increase, renovation work, or both as grounds for this rent increase?
